title: Fore-Mamba3D: Foreground-Enhanced 3D Object Detection
one_liner: This paper makes a 3D object detector faster and more accurate by ignoring background voxels and having foreground voxels share information across regions.
lead: When a 3D sensor scans a scene with a car, a pedestrian, and lots of empty space, most detection models read through every empty space before finding the objects. This paper improves detection speed and accuracy by focusing only on the voxels (tiny 3D blocks) where objects actually are, then letting those voxels talk to each other across regions to fill in missing context.

paras: A 3D object detector must scan a point cloud or voxel grid (a cloud of spatial measurements from a car-mounted laser) and find where the car, pedestrians, and cyclists are. Most modern detectors use a linear encoder called Mamba, which reads every voxel in sequence: empty space, empty space, person, empty space, car, empty space.

The naive approach is to feed all voxels to the encoder. The encoder wastes time on empty space and may get confused by the signal-to-noise ratio (true objects buried in useless background). A beginner might think: just skip the empty voxels and feed only the detected objects. That should be faster because the encoder processes fewer voxels, so fewer computation steps. But when you do this, the objects lose context. A pedestrian alone does not know where the nearby car is or how close the building is. The objects become isolated, and the detector makes mistakes because it cannot relate one object to its neighbors.

callout.html: Reading all voxels is slow but gives context; reading only foreground voxels is fast but leaves each object blind to its neighbors.

steps.text: Run a quick classifier on the raw voxel grid to find likely object locations, keeping only those voxels.
Partition the foreground voxels into spatial chunks so that voxels close together stay together.
Within each region, voxels talk to neighbors; then each region broadcasts its consensus to all other regions so every voxel gains global context.
Combine what-it-is (object class) with where-it-is (position) into a richer representation that Mamba uses.
Mamba encoder processes the enriched foreground sequence and outputs bounding boxes for all objects.

paras: The paper modifies the Mamba encoder's input and internal fusion logic. Instead of feeding all voxels and letting Mamba ignore them, the paper pre-selects foreground voxels (via scoring), groups them spatially, and routes information between regions before Mamba sees them. Then it adds a semantic fusion step inside Mamba so the model learns object identity and location jointly because knowing an object is a car tells it to look for car-like shapes nearby, and knowing it is in a parking lot tells it cars will cluster, so the model's guesses about where one car is influence where it looks for the next.

hidden.h2: Response attenuation: how foreground voxels fade each other
hidden.name: Response attenuation measure
paras: When you feed only foreground voxels to Mamba, each voxel is trying to update its own representation based on all other foreground voxels. But if two foreground voxels are far apart (they come from different objects), the model starts to treat them as unrelated noise. The signal from one object to another weakens because they are sparse and disconnected. The paper calls this response attenuation: the response of the model to a distant foreground voxel decreases because the model spreads its focus thinly across all pairs.

The paper estimates response attenuation implicitly: when foreground voxels are grouped into regions and given a central message (via RGSW), isolated voxels get a boost because now a faraway region's summary arrives as one strong signal instead of many weak individual signals. This improves detection accuracy because when each voxel has the full regional context, it can correctly identify its own object class (is it part of a car or a building) and predict its position correctly.

heat.caption: Darker means stronger signal. Individual isolated voxels fade (1-2); regional summaries stay strong (3-4).

reads.html: When objects are far apart and you only encode them, each object's signal gets weaker because there is no shared message between them. Fore-Mamba3D fixes this by creating a shared regional summary that travels across the scene.

The paper addresses response attenuation in linear attention of foreground sequences via regional-to-global slide window propagation, which ensures that foreground voxels across different instances share contextual information through region-level aggregation.

mechanism.h2: Why it works: the hidden path from foreground to accuracy
paras: Foreground-only encoding isolates objects, but isolation kills context. Mamba's core process (linear attention) has a fixed budget: it can hold one importance-weight-per-voxel-pair. With all voxels, the budget spreads thin (most voxels are background noise). With foreground only, the budget is sharp but the voxels are disconnected.

Fore-Mamba3D reconnects them with two moves. First, RGSW groups nearby foreground voxels and creates a regional summary that propagates to all regions. This is not a weighted averaging of individual signals; it is a discrete regional message (think of it as: region A says I have a car at coordinates X, and that message travels whole to region B). Each voxel then receives this summary, restoring lost context about neighbors because now it knows what other regions detected. Second, SASFMamba fuses semantic labels (is this a car?) with geographic positions (where in space?) inside Mamba so the model can learn that certain object classes appear in certain spatial patterns because cars usually appear in pairs or rows (parking lots, roads) while pedestrians scatter more randomly, so the class label guides the search for similar objects nearby. Together, these prevent the focus from diffusing and ensure every foreground voxel inherits global information without reintroducing background noise.

stages.s: Raw point cloud or voxel grid
Score each voxel for foreground likelihood
RGSW: each region summarizes, broadcasts to all regions
SASFMamba: fuse object class with position
Mamba linear attention on enriched foreground

math.h2: The equation: regional message + detection scoring
math.words: For each region, aggregate foreground voxel features via learned pooling; broadcast aggregated feature to all voxels as a global context vector; concatenate each voxel's local feature with the global context and the semantic class embedding; feed the enriched sequence to Mamba; score each position for object presence.
math.equation: f_enriched_i = concat(f_local_i, f_global_region(i), e_semantic_class_i); h_mamba = Mamba(f_enriched); score_i = W_score * h_mamba_i + b
symbols: the local feature of voxel i from the point cloud
the aggregated feature broadcast from the region containing voxel i
the embedding vector for the object class at voxel i
concatenate three vectors into one long vector
the output sequence from Mamba after processing the enriched features
a learned matrix that rates each Mamba output for object likelihood

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Voxel 1 (car): local feature = [0.5, 0.3], regional summary = [0.8, 0.7], semantic car embedding = [0.9, 0.1]. Concatenate: [0.5, 0.3, 0.8, 0.7, 0.9, 0.1].
Voxel 2 (pedestrian far away, lost in foreground-only): local = [0.2, 0.1], regional summary = [0.6, 0.5], semantic person = [0.4, 0.8]. Concatenate: [0.2, 0.1, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.8].

Without regional summary (old way): voxel 2 sees only [0.2, 0.1, 0.4, 0.8], a weak signal. With regional summary (Fore-Mamba3D): voxel 2 sees [0.2, 0.1, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.8], twice as rich, because it now includes context from its region. Mamba's attention can find the pedestrian.

math.note: The regional summary acts as a carrier of context, so distant foreground voxels no longer fade in isolation; semantic class embedding tells Mamba that cars and people have different patterns, improving discrimination.

bars.h2: Performance comparison: foreground vs. naive foreground

charts.title: Naive foreground-only
charts.note: Foreground-only saves computation because fewer voxels mean fewer arithmetic operations, but loses context because each object no longer sees signals from neighbors, so it cannot relate its identity or position to nearby objects, and detection falls.

charts.title: Fore-Mamba3D
charts.note: RGSW propagation restores context so foreground voxels remain sharp. Semantic fusion improves generalization because the model learns that objects of the same class tend to cluster (cars park together, pedestrians walk in groups), so it can predict one object's location by knowing its class, and when it sees a new scene it knows what to expect.

items.html: If the initial voxel classifier (that picks foreground voxels) is poorly trained or biased, it will miss real objects or include noisy patches. All downstream reasoning is then on a corrupted input.

If regions are oversized, distant objects in the same region pollute each other's summaries (a car at one end confuses voxels at the other). If regions are too small, the RGSW propagation becomes noisy and loses the contextual boost because regional summaries built from few voxels are unstable and carry unreliable information between regions.

items.b: Semantic fusion overfits on one class.
items.html: If the fusion module learns that cars always appear in certain geometric patterns, it will fail on unusual car poses or when cars are occluded by other objects.

When foreground scoring is well-trained, regions are sized to balance local detail with global scope, and semantic fusion sees diverse object instances during training, Fore-Mamba3D recovers the accuracy of full-voxel encoding while keeping the speed of foreground-only encoding.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a toy 3D scene with a known car and pedestrian placement, add random noise points (background), and train a simple Mamba encoder. First, train the naive version that reads all voxels. Record the detection accuracy and how long it takes to process a scene. Then, train Fore-Mamba3D with foreground pre-selection, regional grouping, and semantic fusion. Measure accuracy and processing time again. The demo should show that Fore-Mamba3D matches or beats full-voxel accuracy while processing scenes 3-5 times faster because foreground-only encoding removes the overhead of processing background voxels, and RGSW regional messages restore the context that was lost.
demo.metric_eq: improvement = (accuracy_Fore_Mamba3D - accuracy_naive_foreground) / accuracy_naive_foreground; speedup = time_full_voxel / time_Fore_Mamba3D
demo.closing: The key proof is that adding regional propagation and semantic fusion recovers the lost context, so foreground-only encoding no longer sacrifices accuracy for speed.
